extracted.intended_audience: educated British public, policymakers, and readers interested in constitutional design and the French Revolution
extracted.subtask_description: A polemical essay evaluating the French revolutionary constitution and the institutions it creates, arguing normative standards for representation, monetary policy, executive and legislative design. It offers prescriptive claims about what makes a stable and legitimate government.

rubrics_metrics.name: Representation as representation of the whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Each deputy to the Assembly would be the representative of France, and of all its descriptions, of the many and of the few, of the rich and of the poor, of the great districts and of the small. This standing, unalterable, fundamental government would make ... that territory truly and properly a whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Fragmenting the country into separate republics makes questions of equality and representation useless; representation should regard the whole nation rather than only parts. Representation must originate from and point to a standing, unalterable government serving the whole.

rubrics_metrics.name: Direct connection and accountability between electors and representatives
rubrics_metrics.description: With you the elective Assembly is the sovereign, and the sole sovereign; ... The member who goes to the National Assembly is not chosen by the people, nor accountable to them. There are three elections before he is chosen; two sets of magistracy intervene between him and the primary assembly, so as to render him ... an ambassador of a state, and not the representative of the people within a state.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Multiple intermediary elections sever the link of accountability. A design that inserts two or more bodies between primary electors and representatives changes the spirit of election so the representative cannot be effectively held to account.

rubrics_metrics.name: Electoral mechanisms must enable voters to know candidates and retain influence
rubrics_metrics.description: To answer its real purposes, you must first possess the means of knowing the fitness of your man; and then you must retain some hold upon him by personal obligation or dependence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary electors must be able to judge candidate qualities and to maintain leverage over them; designs that leave primary electors ignorant of candidates' fitness or unable to call them to account nullify meaningful election.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid rules that bar experienced legislators from serving
rubrics_metrics.description: Every man who has served in an assembly is ineligible for two years after. Just as these magistrates begin to learn their trade, like chimney sweepers, they are disqualified for exercising it. Superficial, new, petulant acquisition, and interrupted, dronish, broken, ill recollection is to be the destined character of all your future governors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Temporary ineligibility after service prevents representatives from acquiring and applying experience; continuity and accumulated competence are necessary for effective governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confiscation plus compulsory, unbacked paper currency is unstable and corrosive
rubrics_metrics.description: The first is the confiscation, with the compulsory paper currency annexed to it; ... a paper circulation, not founded on any real money deposited or engaged for ... must put the whole of what power, authority, and influence is left ... into the hands of the managers and conductors of this circulation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While confiscation and paper money may temporarily bind disparate republics, they risk long-term dissociation, collapse of the currency, and concentration of power in monetary managers. Monetary policy must be founded on stable, credible backing to avoid systemic instability and oligarchic control.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not base the commonwealth on speculation or 'gaming' of funds
rubrics_metrics.description: Your legislators, in everything new, are the very first who have founded a commonwealth upon gaming, and infused this spirit into it as its vital breath. The great object in these politics is to metamorphose France from a great kingdom into one great playtable; to turn its inhabitants into a nation of gamesters...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Turning everyday economic life into speculative gambling undermines industry, economy, and prudent provision; government should avoid policies that force subjects into speculative transactions as the core of national life.

rubrics_metrics.name: Currency volatility destroys incentives to labor, saving, and prudent provision
rubrics_metrics.description: Who will labor without knowing the amount of his pay? Who will study to increase what none can estimate? Who will accumulate, when he does not know the value of what he saves?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Uncertain and declining currency value prevents people from planning, working, and saving; stable money is essential to sustain industry, economy, and long‑term provision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid concentration of financial and land power in a single urban center
rubrics_metrics.description: The whole of the power obtained by this revolution will settle in the towns among the burghers and the monied directors who lead them. ... The country gentleman ... will be as completely excluded from the government of his country as if he were legislatively proscribed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When monetary and land-transaction power concentrates in towns (especially a dominant capital), rural actors lack the habits/structures for combination and influence, yielding oligarchic urban dominance and marginalization of the countryside.

rubrics_metrics.name: A republic requires a senate or intermediate council for stability
rubrics_metrics.description: They have forgotten to constitute a senate or something of that nature and character. ... It holds a sort of middle place between the supreme power exercised by the people ... and the mere executive. Of this there are no traces in your constitution, and in providing nothing of this kind ... discovered a sovereign incapacity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An intermediate body gives continuity, a channel for foreign connection, and steadiness in proceedings; omitting such a council exposes a republic to instability and inconsistency.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive must possess dignity, authority, and means to reward to secure faithful service
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive magistracy ought to be constituted in such a manner that those who compose it should be disposed to love and to venerate those whom they are bound to obey. ... It ought to be environed with dignity, authority, and consideration, and it ought to lead to glory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An executive deprived of honor, discretion, and rewards can command only through fear; offices should include incentives (land, pensions, honors) so subordinates have motives beyond mere fear to serve zealously.

rubrics_metrics.name: The sovereign (king) should be the fountain of justice and honor
rubrics_metrics.description: According to the new constitution, the higher parts of judicature ... are not in the king. The king of France is not the fountain of justice. ... He is not even the public prosecutor. He serves only as a notary to authenticate the choice made of the judges.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Stripping the sovereign of visible judicial and honorific functions degrades the office and removes sources of public respect; judicial and honorific roles help sustain the dignity and authority of the executive.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ministers should be chosen by 'affairs' not by affections and must be empowered to act
rubrics_metrics.description: These ministers, who were chosen by affairs, not by affections, acted in the name of, and in trust for, kings, and not as their avowed, constitutional, and ostensible masters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ministers selected for competence and empowered to act in the interest of the state (with means to execute policy) serve the public good; ensuring ministers have real authority (not merely responsibility) is crucial for effective governance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Accountability (responsibility) alone is insufficient to produce active, zealous government
rubrics_metrics.description: It is a poor service that is to be had from responsibility. The elevation of mind to be derived from fear will never make a nation glorious. Responsibility prevents crimes. ... But for a principle of active and zealous service, none but idiots could think of it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Legal responsibility deters misconduct but does not substitute for positive incentives and motivations necessary for vigorous administration; institutions should combine checks with incentives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive must retain prerogatives in foreign policy to command respect
rubrics_metrics.description: Is the conduct of a war to be trusted to a man who may abhor its principle ... Will foreign states seriously treat with him who has no prerogative of peace or war?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the executive cannot make decisions in matters of war and peace, the state will be treated with contempt abroad and divided internally; credible foreign policy requires recognized executive prerogatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political divisions should reflect historic/provincial attachments, not artificial geometry
rubrics_metrics.description: It is boasted that the geometrical policy has been adopted, that all local ideas should be sunk ... No man ever was attached by a sense of pride, partiality, or real affection to a description of square measurement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Constructing provinces by abstract geometrical measures undermines natural local affections and civic attachments; authentic political loyalty grows from family, neighborhood, and historic provincial ties.
